name: Rafael Toral
label: Drag City
lede: Rafael Toral drummed in Lisbon, spent over a decade building his own electronic instruments, then picked the guitar back up and landed at No. 14 on Pitchfork's best of 2024.

eras.title: A Lisbon kid with a volume pedal
eras.text: Toral comes up in Lisbon's post-punk scene, drumming and then playing guitar in bands. After that he goes solo at home with a four-track, a first guitar and an 8-bit delay, and the recordings sit unreleased for years.

years.src: Resident Advisor: Rafael Toral biography · Tiny Mix Tapes: Rafael Toral interview · The Quietus: The Strange World Of... Rafael Toral
years.h: Rafael Toral is a Lisbon drummer first
years.p: Resident Advisor's bio has him performing as a drummer from 1984, years before anyone called him a guitarist.
years.xp:
Resident Advisor gives his birth year as 1967 in Lisbon. He tells The Quietus he learned Beatles songs on acoustic guitar at 12 and became fixated on what an electric guitar could do as a teenager.

In a Tiny Mix Tapes interview he says he decided to be a musician at 16, after hearing Bauhaus and Cocteau Twins on a Portuguese radio show.

years.src: Bandcamp Daily: Where to Start with Portuguese Experimentalist Rafael Toral · Tone Glow 125: Rafael Toral · The Fader: A morning in Rafael Toral's garden of drone
years.h: He plays guitar in Pop Dell'Arte and SPQR
years.p: Bandcamp Daily lists Pop Dell'Arte, No Noise Reduction and SPQR, the last with [[João Paulo Feliciano|876f19c4-c33e-4397-8942-02328058a52b]], among his first bands.
years.xp:
Sources disagree on the details: Bandcamp Daily also names the avant-pop group Mler Ife Dada, while Tone Glow dates his joining Pop Dell'Arte to 1985. The Fader describes Pop Dell'Arte as a Portuguese punk band.

Tone Glow cites Echo and the Bunnymen, Bauhaus and Cocteau Twins as the sound he was chasing.

years.src: Tone Glow 125: Rafael Toral · The Quietus: The Strange World Of... Rafael Toral · The Fader: A morning in Rafael Toral's garden of drone
years.h: SPQR falls apart, so Toral records alone
years.p: Tone Glow dates his solo work from summer 1987.
years.xp:
The Quietus describes the early material as home recordings on a 4-track cassette machine, with his first guitar, a volume pedal and an 8-bit delay. It came out only in 2001 as Early Works, covering 1987 to 1990.

The Fader reports he now considers his 1994 debut derivative.

eras.title: Seven years on one record
eras.text: Toral puts out guitar-and-electronics albums under his own name and falls in with Jim O'Rourke and the free-improvising ensemble MIMEO. The decade closes with a record that takes seven years to finish.

years.src: The Quietus: The Strange World Of... Rafael Toral · Drag City: Rafael Toral · The Fader: A morning in Rafael Toral's garden of drone
years.h: Sound Mind Sound Body is the debut he now shrugs off
years.p: His first solo album is built around the guitar-signal-chain piece "AER 7 E"; he names John Cage, Alvin Lucier and Brian Eno as influences.
years.xp:
Drag City's catalog shows the album reissued in 2001, 2018 and 2025. The Quietus interview places "AER 7 E" at its center.

Toral told The Fader the synth-based record now feels derivative to him, which has not stopped three reissues.

years.src: The Quietus: The Strange World Of... Rafael Toral · Bandcamp Daily: Where to Start with Portuguese Experimentalist Rafael Toral
years.h: A Buzzcocks concert sets off Wave Field
years.p: Two long pieces that Bandcamp Daily says were recorded in a single afternoon, with My Bloody Valentine and Eno as reference points.
years.xp:
The Quietus interview ties the record's vision to a Buzzcocks concert and lists Lucier, Eno and My Bloody Valentine as influences.

That year he also met [[Nicolas Collins|f7a5c31b-fd2c-4fc3-8f1e-82be21683d05]] at STEIM in Amsterdam and learned circuit design from him, per The Quietus.

years.src: The Quietus: The Strange World Of... Rafael Toral · Bandcamp Daily: Where to Start with Portuguese Experimentalist Rafael Toral · Tiny Mix Tapes: Rafael Toral interview
years.h: [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] puts Toral onto the modular synthesizer
years.p: Toral says the Chicago musician introduced him to modular synths in 1997, and the two recorded together that year.
years.xp:
Those 1997-era sessions sat in a drawer until 2010, when they came out as Electronic Music, credited to Toral and O'Rourke.

Toral calls O'Rourke one of his dearest friends in a Tiny Mix Tapes interview.

years.src: The Quietus: The Strange World Of... Rafael Toral · Bandcamp Daily: Where to Start with Portuguese Experimentalist Rafael Toral
years.h: Aeriola Frequency turns feedback loops into an album
years.p: The Quietus describes Toral's 1998 record as electronic resonance drawn from feedback-loop circuits.

years.cap: Violence of Discovery and Calm of Acceptance, Touch TO:48
years.src: Touch: TO:48 Violence of Discovery and Calm of Acceptance · Bandcamp Daily: Where to Start with Portuguese Experimentalist Rafael Toral
years.h: Seven years on ten guitar pieces: Violence of Discovery and Calm of Acceptance
years.p: His first album for Touch runs from 1993 to 2000 in the making, and Touch says every sound came from electric guitars and analog gear.
years.xp:
Touch's catalog page says ten tracks, with the only outside sound the background noise on the last track, taken from a Space Shuttle webcast. Reviewers there compare the guitar textures to bowed wineglasses, distant choirs and underwater harps.

Touch lists Toral's collaborators as including John Zorn, [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]], Jim O'Rourke and [[Phill Niblock|12e4406c-33db-4414-92bb-f63b4602a7f4]].

years.src: Bandcamp Daily: Where to Start with Portuguese Experimentalist Rafael Toral · Tiny Mix Tapes: Rafael Toral interview · AllMusic: Rafael Toral
years.h: MIMEO puts a Bologna set on record with John Tilbury
years.p: The Hands of Caravaggio was recorded at the AngelicA festival in May 2000 with pianist [[John Tilbury|3a3c6d0a-c1f6-4198-a8f4-93c8ae6678dd]], and Toral had joined the free-improvising ensemble in the late 1990s.
years.xp:
MIMEO counted [[Keith Rowe|84b993bd-2743-48b0-88fb-88ebbe89789b]] and Christian Fennesz among its members. Toral credits Rowe with teaching him economy: justify every sound you play.

The group followed with Lifting Concrete Lightly in 2004.

eras.title: The guitar goes down, the Space Program starts
eras.text: Around 2003 or 2004 Toral sets the guitar aside and builds his own electronic instruments, meaning to play them the way a jazz musician plays a horn, with silence as part of the music. The project runs for the better part of fifteen years.

years.cap: Rafael Toral live at A Square Art Space, October 5, 2004
years.src: Drag City: Toral Histories · Tiny Mix Tapes: Rafael Toral interview · AllMusic: Rafael Toral · The Quietus: The Strange World Of... Rafael Toral
years.h: Toral builds electronics to play like a jazz horn
years.p: His aim, in his words, was electronic music more concerned with the musician than with the instrument; AllMusic dates the shift to 2003.
years.xp:
The instruments included glove-controlled computer sine waves, a modified pocket amplifier and a theremin-controlled feedback circuit. [[Sei Miguel|1e7228a2-92fa-4dfd-aeb1-2f138cc08169]], the Lisbon trumpeter, is the collaborator Toral credits most for shaping his system, and he challenged him to develop the modified pocket amplifier.

Drag City counts six albums plus workshops and performances across the project, which ran to 2017.

years.cap: Toral at the Wire 25 concert, Bush Hall, London, November 17, 2007
years.src: The Quietus: The Strange World Of... Rafael Toral · Drag City: Toral Histories
years.h: Space introduces "post-free jazz electronic music"
years.p: The record is built from live performances of 2004 and 2005, with Sei Miguel on trumpet and Fala Mariam on trombone.
years.xp:
The Quietus credits Miles Davis and his handling of silence as a model for the record.

Toral has said of the project: "What I'm doing, as far as I know, has never been done before."

years.cap: Rafael Toral on stage at Kings Place, London, September 2009
years.src: Drag City: Rafael Toral · Resident Advisor: Rafael Toral biography
years.h: Space Elements takes three volumes to chart the instruments
years.p: Drag City's catalog and Resident Advisor both list the 2008-2011 trilogy, the core of the Space Program's recorded output.

years.cap: Toral live at Fleisenberg Floft, March 3, 2011
years.src: Resident Advisor: Rafael Toral biography · The Fader: A morning in Rafael Toral's garden of drone
years.h: He moves to the mountains of Portugal
years.p: Resident Advisor says Toral relocated in 2014 to live more sustainably.
years.xp: The Fader adds that in his early forties he took up Zen meditation and Wing Chun, and describes his electronic performing as an awareness of the movements involved.

years.src: Resident Advisor: Rafael Toral biography · Drag City: Toral Histories
years.h: Space Solo 2 ends the Space Program, 13 years in
years.p: Resident Advisor calls it the program's last project.

eras.title: Back toward the guitar
eras.text: With the Space Program wound down, Toral brings jazz phrasing and harmony into his work and, slowly, the guitar. Collaborations with percussionists and small ensembles fill the gap before the next solo record.

years.src: Resident Advisor: Rafael Toral biography · AllMusic: Rafael Toral · The Quietus: The Strange World Of... Rafael Toral
years.h: Moon Field opens what Toral calls a new phase
years.p: Resident Advisor places the album in 2018, blending jazz-influenced phrasing with broader soundscapes; AllMusic dates it 2017.
years.xp: He also released Jupiter and Beyond with the Portuguese percussionist and gong maker João Pais Filipe in 2018, per The Quietus and the Tone Glow interview.

years.src: The Quietus: The Strange World Of... Rafael Toral
years.h: Constellation in Still Time borrows John Cage's methods
years.p: Toral's generative piece extends "AER 7" with Cage's composition techniques, per The Quietus.
years.xp:
The Quietus lists clavinet, harp, piano and vibraphone among its sounds.

The video is a full 16-minute Toral set from the Semibreve festival in 2021, a few years after the record.

eras.title: A garden of drone
eras.text: After more than a decade of self-built electronics, Toral returns to the electric guitar. The record comes out on Jim O'Rourke's Moikai label with Drag City handling the release, and the critics show up.

years.src: Drag City: Toral Histories
years.h: Drag City sells "Second Short Space" as aurora borealis in daylight
years.p: The third advance single from Spectral Evolution arrives with that description of its sound.

years.cap: Toral playing guitar in green stage light, November 2024
years.src: Drag City: Spectral Evolution · A Closer Listen: Rafael Toral, Spectral Evolution · The Fader: A morning in Rafael Toral's garden of drone · Drag City: Rafael Toral
years.h: Spectral Evolution brings the guitar back, with birdsong by theremin
years.p: Twelve episodes play as one 47-minute piece, built on chord changes taken from jazz standards.
years.xp:
Drag City says the record marks Toral's return to electric guitar after over a decade exclusively with self-built electronic modules. A Closer Listen reports the changes in several pieces derive from classic jazz chords by George Gershwin and Duke Ellington.

The Fader reports the bird-like sounds come from a feedback path controlled by a theremin antenna, the same gear used on the Space Program records. He describes the album as a parallel between a record and a garden.

years.src: Album of the Year: Spectral Evolution · Igloo Magazine: Rafael Toral, Spectral Evolution
years.h: Pitchfork gives it an 8.0, The Guardian a perfect score
years.p: Pitchfork's Matthew Blackwell called Spectral Evolution an explosive re-entry into the atmosphere; Album of the Year lists Pitchfork at 80/100.
years.xp:
Album of the Year's critic page also shows The Guardian at 100, Spectrum Culture at 95, Uncut at 90 and Mojo at 80, with an aggregate critic score of 89 from five reviews.

Igloo Magazine compared the slow chord progressions to Stars of the Lid.

years.src: Rafael Toral: Spectral Evolution on Best of 2024 · Rafael Toral (official site)
years.h: Pitchfork ranks it No. 14 of 2024, The Wire No. 2
years.p: Toral's own site logs Spectral Evolution at No. 14 at Pitchfork, No. 7 at The Quietus and No. 2 at The Wire; Stereogum put it first on its experimental list.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's list of the 50 best albums of 2024 put it at No. 14, per Toral's site and the year-end listing.

Sources disagree on the release date: Drag City and Album of the Year say February 23, while some review sites say March. The page uses Drag City's date.

years.src: Drag City: Rafael Toral
years.h: A live Spectral Evolution follows on Noise Precision Library
years.p: Drag City's artist page lists a live recording of the album issued in 2025.

q: I treated them as sublime sound entities.
years.src: Rafael Toral (official site) · The Quietus: The Strange World Of... Rafael Toral · Drag City: Rafael Toral
years.h: Traveling Light premieres at the Venice Biennale
years.p: Toral on the jazz standards behind the album, which gets its live premiere in Venice on October 11, before its October 24 release.
years.xp:
Toral's site calls it his 28th release, with "Easy Living" as the first single on September 3. Per The Quietus, the ensemble includes saxophonist [[Rodrigo Amado|63dc2a62-587a-43cd-93fe-45f7151bb8da]], flugelhorn player Yaw Tembe, clarinetist José Bruno Parrinha and flutist Clara Saleiro.

He told The Quietus: "I'm aware of the tradition in jazz to deconstruct, reinvent or improvise over standards and I didn't want to reinvent anything."
